Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday. Storix legal and infosec want a clear handoff plan that covers: SSO (SAML metadata + IdP attributes), SCIM attribute mapping for groups and roles, a scoped set of service accounts for event ingestion, and an IP allowlist for our private endpoints.

A couple asks to start:
- Can you confirm recommended service account naming and minimum scopes for ingestion & audits?
- We prefer SCIM: externalId->employee_id mapping and group->team attribute for role sync; can you validate?
- We'll provide an IP range but want a formal allowlist declaration for our audit docs.

Goal is to complete the handoff checklist and run a 1-hour tech kickoff next week. Please CC whoever from your onboarding/implementation team.

Thanks,

Jared — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (CS/implementation) and Kimberly (security/compliance) to own the technical checklists. High level answers:

- Service accounts: we recommend three scoped SAs for your integration: ingestion-sa (write-only to streaming endpoints + write audit logs), admin-read-sa (read-only for troubleshooting), and audit-sa (append-only to audit store). We'll send a naming and scope doc.
- SCIM mappings: externalId->employee_id and "groups"->teams is supported; we typically recommend a canonical "redwood_role" claim derived from group membership for RBAC mapping on our side.
- IP allowlist: we can accept a CIDR block list and emit a signed allowlist declaration for your audit package. We ask that customer-managed IPs be stable during cutover; small changes are OK but must be scheduled.

Proposed next step: 1-hour tech kickoff on Thu Mar 18 10:00 PT. Monica — can you prepare the SCIM attribute template and the SA naming PDF? Kimberly — can you prepare the compliance checklist (SOC2 artifacts + allowlist declaration)?

Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jared — attaching the SCIM attribute CSV we use in practice (storix-scim-attributes-v1.csv). Quick notes:

- Required user attrs: userName, externalId, active, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work].value
- Group sync: groups.displayName -> redwood_role (we can also map to customAttribute:team if you prefer)
- For staged rollout we recommend a group-based canary (create a "redwood-canary" group in your IdP).

Service account guidance (attached PDF):
- ingestion-sa: principle-of-least-privilege, token TTL 7d, rotation via KMS automated job
- admin-read-sa: read-only, audit-only logging allowed
- audit-sa: append-only to audit topic, additional MFA policy for token creation

I also attached an IP allowlist template (ip-allowlist-declaration.yaml). Jared, if you reply with your CIDRs we will generate a signed declaration and include it in the SOC2 packet.

Action items assigned:
- Jared: send the initial CIDR(s) and preferred SCIM user attribute for externalId (Helen?) — due Mon Mar 15.
- Kimberly: confirm whether Storix requires an auditor-signed copy of the allowlist — due Mon Mar 15.
- Priyom: create the HubSpot checklist and add the DocuSign envelope for the connectivity attestation.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Jared / team — quick compliance clarifications:

- Allowlist provenance: for SOC2 we typically provide a signed YAML (see Monica's template) plus a change-log CSV when you update ranges. If your auditors need an "auditor-signed" doc we can coordinate with our compliance team but usually a signed Redwood declaration + change log suffices.
- Service account entropy & rotation: we require HSM-backed key rotation for audit-sa tokens; ingestion-sa may use shorter TTL tokens (recommended 7 days) with automated rotation.
- Org policies: if Storix enforces conditional access (e.g., only allow API creation from RBAC admin group) let us know — we can map a configuration policy in the console.

I'll be on the kickoff call to validate the allowlist output and sign-off the SA scopes.

Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
